scope: Existing R4/R5/R6/R8/R9 operational launch, continuation, repaired-entry durability, and independent result uploads; R1 detailed audit delegated separately

concrete_findings.trigger: Repeat the old R9 thin online launcher after backend_entry.py has received the authorized runtime repair
concrete_findings.behavior: verify_install raises Installed file hash mismatch; refusing to overwrite: runtime/backend_entry.py
concrete_findings.affected: Manual recovery through original pinned installers that hash an operational entry changed by the authorized repair; original R4/R5/R6/R8 installers have the same verification design
concrete_findings.repair: resume_existing.py reads the saved plan and saved launch and invokes the installed original controller_loop; it does not call an installer or prepare_context

verified_behaviors: Three independent single-GPU requests retain their round-specific partition, CPU, memory and marker
Submission retries handle QOS limit rejection without cancelling existing workers or sending three identical rejected requests
Lost sbatch acknowledgement is adopted by durable exact attempt name; ambiguous submissions retain occupancy to avoid duplication
Worker USR1 reaches the native child, waits for cooperative checkpoint completion, and returns75
A finished worker with exit75 is resubmitted after evidence is observed; per-job time limit is5days3hours, not a cumulative12hour ceiling
A local terminal outcome covers sacct propagation delay while live queue evidence always prevents premature duplication
Native .lock and task leases protect numerical outputs and checkpoint files across supervisor/node loss
Result monitor, report dispatcher, paper upload and archive upload run independently and do not control the numerical training process
Compute backend starts only existing installed packages and verified node cache paths; no pip, package download or full-data rescan is invoked
Recovery immediately reuses held controller and upload/monitor locks without spawning duplicate components
Recovery accepts original R5/R6/R8/R9 coordinator context in fresh isolated processes without prepare_context or resource reconstruction
Recovery does not start or migrate R1/R4, since those distinct recovery interfaces were outside this helper's validated scope
availability_limits: An unavailable Slurm queue or accounting service causes controller observation retry; existing numerical workers continue independently, but replacement submission may wait for the service
An accepted submission whose acknowledgement and accounting evidence are both permanently lost cannot be retried safely without duplicate-job risk; current implementation waits for evidence
Physical node failure, scheduler intervention, filesystem outage or exhausted disk cannot be ruled out by software-only validation
The helper is supplied but not installed or run on the school server by this audit
